summary.headline: Arvind Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 23% to INR2,919 crores and EBITDA rose 27% to INR331 crores, both all-time quarterly highs, with margin held at 11.4%.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue and EBITDA, with the advanced materials business (including Dalco-GFT for a full quarter) the main growth driver. Textile margins were hit by raw material inflation (75 bps), and management said pass-through to customers still lags cost escalation. Net debt fell by about INR95 crores to INR2,063 crores despite a temporary working capital build. Management guided to mid-teens garmenting growth and 18%+ advanced materials growth in Q3 FY27, while stating that the cost environment remains uncertain.

segments.name: Textile (denim, woven, knits)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,999 crores (+11%) and EBITDA INR190 crores; denim volume above 18 million meters (+19% YoY, highest in 17 quarters); woven volume 34 million meters. Input costs cut margin by 75 bps.

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR577 crores (+9%) on better mix and realisation; volume crossed 11 million pieces for the second quarter running, up about 4%. Knits export demand was soft in H1.

segments.name: Advanced materials
segments.commentary: Record revenue INR805 crores (+81%), EBITDA margin 14.8%. India business INR550 crores (+23%) led by human protection and composites; industrial segment lost about one and a half quarters of production due to logistics delays on imported investments.

guidance_outlook: Garmenting expected to deliver mid-teens revenue growth for FY27, with a stronger H2 (management said H2 garmenting growth should be better than 11% and full-year around 15%).
Advanced materials expected to grow 18%+ in Q3 FY27.
Growth capex above INR500 crores in FY27: about INR200 crores advanced materials, INR120-150 crores garmenting, balance fabric and maintenance. Dalco capex is separate (about USD 5 million a year).
Margin expected to be maintained in advanced materials through sourcing, productivity and pricing; long-run goal of about 50 bps EBITDA margin improvement per year (margin was about 11.5% last year).

Long-term debt to stay at pre-Dalco level of about INR400 crores; working capital debt to grow with business at 6+ turns, targeting 7 over a couple of years. ECB of about INR600 crores (India) due for repayment in May 2027 using QIP proceeds.
Varanasi Phase 1 (essentials and knits) expected to deliver double-digit EBITDA and 20%+ ROCE once scaled, after 6-8 months of ramp-up.
capex_capacity: Denim in-house capacity about 70 million meters per annum; woven capacity about 140-150 million meters per annum. Denim is close to full utilisation; brownfield debottlenecking and external asset-light capacity tied up for near term.

Varanasi greenfield garmenting Phase 1 commissioned: revenue potential INR250 crores, capex INR75 crores including land; about 25 million essentials pieces, not counted in the 50 million garment base.
Woven: doubled corduroy capacity and adding flannel capacity to even out seasonality; about 10% additional fabric capacity via low-cost machine upgrades.
A fourth line with INR70 crores annual revenue potential was commissioned in Q2 and was fully sold before investment.
Carbon pultrusion and weaving capacity added in advanced materials; carbon targeted at 20-30% of overall product in 3-4 years; contributing only tens of crores initially.
US garmenting: next line being invested in this year; target mid-teens US growth reached in the year after next. Utilisation described as very high.
demand_pricing: Demand described as reasonably robust in textiles and advanced materials; US order book for Q3 'extremely strong' and Q4 building.

Pricing: pass-through is done quarterly and lags cost escalations; 75-100 bps of gross margin erosion each quarter is being fought back. Dalco says new prices accepted by many customers from September.
Realisations in fabric and woven up about 20%, with price pass-through as the main driver and product mix secondary.
India-UK FTA: UK sourcing enquiries rising; first benefits expected in Q4 FY27, with UK business about 10-12 million garments higher next year (garment-only).
Defence: combat and officer uniforms are consumables with renewable reorder cycles; new Indian defence orders won in the quarter. Data centres driving US composite demand.
Ruf & Tuf denim brand is dormant; management has no current plan for a B2C play.

qa_highlights.question: Why is garmenting volume growth only about 4%, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 was soft in knits export and some categories, leaving spare knit capacity. H2 is expected to be stronger on denim, essentials and seasonality, with revenue growth guided to mid-teens rather than piece count.

qa_highlights.question: Is the denim growth cyclical and sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the business is now more focused and less commodity-linked, citing design and innovation investment, studios in London and Amsterdam, a third US studio planned, and multi-country sourcing (Bangladesh, Egypt, with Egypt's first denim deliveries in Q3).

qa_highlights.question: How will raw material and logistics costs be passed on, and how often?
qa_highlights.answer: Pass-through is reviewed every quarter, and management said it lags cost increases. Demand destruction limits how far prices can rise. Logistics is largely borne by about 18% of customers on their terms.

qa_highlights.question: What are the finance cost and debt-reduction plans after the rating upgrade and QIP?
qa_highlights.answer: A 25 bps benefit from the rating upgrade, though RBI repo hikes of about 50 bps are expected over two quarters. Management expects debt to fall from Q1 FY28 once the May 2027 ECB is repaid from QIP funds; long-term debt is to remain at about INR400 crores pre-Dalco level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR500 crore capex inclusive of Dalco and how quickly does capex ramp?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR500 crore capex is India-only; Dalco has its own program. Management said capex takes about two years to ramp fully, at asset turnover of 2.5-3x.

qa_highlights.question: What is the garmenting expansion plan beyond the 15% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is exploring a larger garment greenfield, with a 25% growth model on the drawing board to be launched in a few quarters. For the next 3-4 quarters the focus is brownfield plus the one or two greenfields already started.

risks_watch: Raw material, petrochemical and freight inflation are running ahead of price pass-through; management says there is no visible let-up.
Working capital is elevated by inventory bought ahead at fixed prices; working capital turns must stay at 6 or better.
Rising RBI repo rates may offset the rating-driven finance cost benefit.
Dependence on RoSCTL export incentive (extended to December); management did not quantify its share of revenue or EBITDA.
Industrial advanced materials ramp after about 1.5 quarters of logistics-related production delay; Dalco margins compressed by petrochemical inputs.
Knit export demand softness and under-utilised knit capacity in H1.
The May 2027 ECB repayment and the timing of the UK FTA benefit in Q4 FY27 are key milestones.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and execution, with a record quarter and upgraded rating, but cautious on costs. Management repeatedly said raw material and logistics escalations are outpacing pass-through and that the outlook is 'cautiously optimistic'. Some answers were vague on quantities (RoSCTL exposure, Varanasi margins beyond double-digit).
key_quotes: Let me begin by saying that this has been a record quarter for Arvind and it has come in what has clearly been another year of disruption.
So, while number of pieces might go up less, the turnover will go up higher than the number of pieces.
But this every quarter, there is some new escalation that is happening.
The 60 million is what will get paid back in May, which is why the QIP proceeds were sort of brought into the company.

growth.why: Management guides garmenting to mid-teens FY27 growth (H2 above 11%, full year around 15%) and advanced materials to 18%+ in Q3 FY27, backed by Varanasi Phase 1, a fourth line, a US order book described as extremely strong for Q3, and pass-through pricing (fabric realisations up about 20%), but no order-level numbers were given for the garmenting guide and denim is near full capacity.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management targets about 50 bps EBITDA margin gain a year (FY27 base about 11.5%), but Q2 textile margin fell 75 bps and pass-through lags cost by 75-100 bps a quarter.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Varanasi Phase 1 and a fourth garmenting line are already commissioned, and the next US garmenting line is planned for about 4 quarters out; denim is near full use at about 70m meters capacity against 18m meters a quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Garmenting volume grew only about 4% in H1 but management guides H2 garmenting above 11% and full year around 15%, and advanced materials 18%+ in Q3 FY27 with a US Q3 order book called extremely strong.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is very close to full capacity and exploring a larger garment greenfield with a 25% growth model to launch in a few quarters, after more than INR500 crore growth capex in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Garmenting guide is mid-teens for FY27 and advanced materials 18%+ in Q3, but cost headwinds are running ahead of pass-through, so an upgrade depends on the cost environment.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material, petrochemical and freight inflation is ahead of pass-through with no visible let-up, and RBI repo hikes of about 50 bps are expected, while RoSCTL export incentive (extended to December) exposure was not quantified.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Varanasi Phase 1 (essentials and knits) ramps over 6-8 months and the UK FTA benefit starts Q4 FY27 with UK business about 10-12 million garments higher next year; carbon composites targeted at 20-30% of product in 3-4 years.

rows.label: Debt reduction after May 2027 ECB repayment
rows.why: Net debt fell about INR95 crore to INR2,063 crore and the INR600 crore ECB is due May 2027 to be repaid from QIP proceeds, with long-term debt held at about INR400 crore.

rows.label: Advanced materials India ramp after logistics delay
rows.why: Industrial segment lost about 1.5 quarters of production to logistics delays on imported investments, so a catch-up is possible once equipment arrives; advanced materials India revenue was INR550 crore, up 23%.

rows.label: Quarterly price pass-through catch-up
rows.why: Fabric realisations rose about 20% and Dalco says customers accepted new prices from September, but management says pass-through still lags the 75-100 bps quarterly margin erosion.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, record revenue and EBITDA, the rating upgrade and the US order book, but cautious on raw material and logistics costs that are running ahead of pass-through; analysts pushed on garmenting volume growth of only about 4%, RoSCTL exposure and the finance cost impact
